_readme: THE PROVIDER REGISTER — [pipeline K-5] company/pipeline/08-compliance-legal.md
Every third party that touches a payment, a user's data, or the delivery of the Services: what role
it plays, whether the published pages name it, and — the field the whole file hangs off — whether it
is REACHABLE IN CODE today.
WHY IT EXISTS. K-5 says 'the commercial surface names the actual seller and payment path'. Nothing
compared the two. At the moment this register landed the three published pages and the code disagreed
in four independent places, and no build anywhere could go red over any of them:
· services/subly-api/src/routes/webhooks.ts declares POST /revenuecat. RevenueCat is named in no
published page and in no ADR.
· [ADR 004] LOCKED Paddle as the merchant of record on 2026-07-23. Paddle is named in none of
privacy.html, terms.html or refund.html. ✅ HALF FIXED — terms.html §4 and refund.html §2/§4 now
name Paddle and describe the merchant-of-record role ([ADR 039]). privacy.html still says only
'a merchant of record' and is the remaining half, because that page is inside the policy-VERSION
surface: correcting it is a version bump plus an archive snapshot (assert-policy-archive.mjs),
which is one owner signature covering every privacy.html correction at once, not three.
· terms.html and refund.html say website purchases are processed by Razorpay, while privacy.html
says 'We do not sell anything directly from this website today'. The pages contradict each other.
✅ FIXED — the `website-seller-contradiction` gap was retired when the wording landed. All three
pages now agree that nothing is sold directly from the website yet; the two that are not version-
gated additionally name the seller that will take the payment.
· privacy.html says usage statistics AND CRASH REPORTS run on infrastructure provided by
Cloudflare. Crash reports run on Oracle Cloud (company/runbooks/glitchtip.md).
🔴 EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS FIXED BY EDITING A PUBLISHED LEGAL PAGE, WHICH IS OWNER WORK (OWNER_QUEUE
O-3). They are therefore carried as `disclosureGap` rows that PRINT on every run — never silently
exempted, and never made a build failure, because failing CI on copy only the owner can write blocks
every other lane on this repository. tooling/ci/assert-policy-claims.mjs FAILS the moment a gap row's
stated reason stops being true, so an exemption cannot outlive what it was granted for.
⚠️ WHAT IS PUBLIC HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. This is a public repository. A row records the provider's
NAME, its ROLE, where the code reaches it and whether a page discloses it. It records nothing about
the merchant account itself — no merchant ids, no KYC state, no bank or payout details, no contract
terms. Those live in the private SSoT and a row points at them by NAME only, in `privateRecord`,
the same split tooling/channel-register.json uses for signing custody. See tooling/legal/README.md.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-policy-claims.mjs:
· every claims row typed `provider` resolves to a row here                        [K-5]
· every row with `reachableAt` names a route path that really exists in services/  [K-5]
· every route path segment in services/** is either a provider row's tell or is
named in `nonProviderRouteSegments` below — so a NEW payment webhook cannot be
added without somebody writing its name down                                     [K-5]
· a `merchant_of_record` row with status `live` MUST be named in BOTH terms.html
and refund.html; one that is not yet live PRINTS with its owner item             [K-5]
· every `disclosureGap` row carries an ownerItem and a `stillTrue` probe, and the
guard FAILS when the probe stops matching — the gap is resolved, retire the row   [C-6 split]
· COVERAGE LOST on an empty register or zero route paths extracted                 [F-10]
And by tooling/ci/assert-sink-disclosure.mjs — THE SINK-DISCLOSURE LIMB:
· every `infrastructure` row with status `live` DECLARES the personal-data
categories it receives and retains (`receives`), with a stated `receivesBasis`   [K-5]
· every published "we do not collect / do not store X" denial is SCOPED against
the union of those declarations, and FAILS when a live sink declares what a
page denies                                                                      [K-5]
· a denial that resolves to NO declared category FAILS unless it is classified
in `denialsOutOfScope` — a new denial cannot be published unscoped               [K-5]
· COVERAGE LOST on zero live infrastructure rows, an empty declared union, or
zero denials extracted from the pages                                            [F-10]

_why: 🔴 THIS IS THE HALF THAT MAKES THE ROUTE LIMB UNFAKEABLE, and it is data rather than a list
inside the guard on purpose. The guard extracts every literal path segment registered in
services/**/src/**/*.ts. A segment is allowed to exist only if it is either a provider row's
tell (RevenueCat's `/revenuecat`) or is written down HERE as a resource of ours.
So adding `app.post('/paddle', …)` — or `/stripe`, or `/lemonsqueezy` — turns the build RED
until somebody either adds the provider row or claims the segment as ours. There is no third
option and no way to pad the allowlist except by naming the thing you are adding.
⚠️ `:param` segments are dropped before the comparison, not listed here: `/:id` and `/:app` are
placeholders, and listing them would be listing the syntax rather than a resource.
_money: 🟢 `money` WAS ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT — the second time in two days, on a change that
had already passed every other guard. services/platform/src/routes/money.ts mounts
POST /v1/money/:provider ([pipeline 5]M-1, the merchant-of-record webhook) and CI went red naming
a segment nobody had classified. `money` is OURS: it is the door, not a vendor.
⚠️ AND THE PROVIDER IS A `:param`, WHICH THIS LIMB DROPS BY DESIGN. So adding Lemon Squeezy's
adapter tomorrow adds NO new literal segment, and the K-5 property this limb exists for — 'a new
payment webhook cannot land without somebody writing its name down' — would not fire here. That
is not a hole, and it is not left to a comment either: the provider set is DATA in
now FAILS when a registered rail has no row in THIS FILE. The obligation moved to the register
that actually knows the provider set, rather than being satisfied by a URL shape.
Paddle's row keeps `reachableAt: null` deliberately: the reverse check requires the last segment
of `reachableAt` to appear as a LITERAL route segment somewhere in services/**, and `paddle` never
does — it is resolved from the registry at request time. Claiming `/v1/money/paddle` would make
this file assert something no route registration says.
_account: 🟢 `account` WAS ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT IT, which is the whole point and worth recording.
services/platform/src/routes/account.ts (DELETE /v1/account, [pipeline B-5]) landed on main WHILE
this register was being written. The guard went red on the next run naming the new segment: a route
nobody had classified as ours or as a provider's. It is ours — the erasure route — so it is claimed
here rather than given a provider row. That is the limb working on a real, unplanned change on its
first day, rather than on a fixture.
_plan: 🟢 `plan` AND `cancel` WERE ADDED BECAUSE THIS LIMB CAUGHT THEM — the third time in three days,
on a change that had already passed every other guard. services/platform/src/routes/cancellation.ts
mounts POST /v1/plan/cancel ([pipeline 5]M-9, the ROSCA cancel path) and CI went red naming two
Both are OURS and neither is a vendor tell. `plan` is the thing the user bought, in the chassis's
own vocabulary — deliberately not "subscription", which [pipeline C-10] bans from shared code as
apps/subly's domain noun. `cancel` is the verb. No merchant of record is named in either, and none
can be: the route resolves the subscription from the verified session, never from the request.

roles._why: The vocabulary rows are validated against, declared once HERE rather than inside the guard — the same reason keyKinds lives in tooling/channel-register.json. Renaming a role out from under the rows still using it fails.
roles.store_billing: an app store that sells to the user and pays us. It is the seller of record for that sale and we never see the card.
roles.merchant_of_record: the legal seller for anything sold outside an app store. It collects and remits sales tax worldwide and is who the buyer contracted with.
roles.payment_gateway: processes a card payment on our behalf. NOT the seller — we remain the seller, and the tax duty stays with us.
roles.iap_aggregator: normalises store purchase events into one entitlement feed. Holds purchase state, not payment instruments.
roles.infrastructure: runs or hosts the Services. Sees traffic and whatever the Services store, and is disclosed as a processor rather than as a seller.
roles.identity: authenticates users and holds account credentials.
roles.email_delivery: sends the transactional email the Services generate — sign-in links, verification. Holds the recipient address in order to deliver to it, and is disclosed as a processor. NOT a marketing channel: a mailing list is a separate purpose with its own consent (ConsentPurpose.marketingEmail) and would be its own disclosure.

_why: 🔴 THE SINK VOCABULARY. Declared HERE and not inside the guard, for the same reason `roles` above is:
renaming a category out from under the rows still using it must FAIL rather than quietly mean nothing.
WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL, and it is worth stating in full because the defect it answers was PUBLISHED.
privacy.html said 'We do not collect or store your IP address'. The self-hosted GlitchTip on the Oracle
box was storing `user.ip_address`, re-observed on two independent events. NO GUARD COULD SEE IT:
· assert-policy-claims.mjs compares published TEXT to repo TEXT — it can prove the site says what
the repo says and nothing more, and both false statements passed it;
· the one claim row that IS typed `code` asserts `absent(cf-connecting-ip)` over ONE file, and its
own `why` concedes it 'is not a dataflow proof';
· tooling/legal/data-inventory.json declares 19 stores and EVERY ONE is Cloudflare D1 or KV. The
strings `glitchtip`, `oracle`, `sentry` and `ip_address` appear nowhere in it. The only
personal-data store outside Cloudflare was invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.
This register is the one artifact that already knew the crash rail is `oracle-cloud · infrastructure ·
live`. So the declaration is attached to the thing that knows the sink exists.
`tells` are how a category is recognised in a PUBLISHED DENIAL — the words a reader would see, not the
column names. They are matched against the text AFTER the denial verb, so 'We receive confirmation of
the purchase but do not collect or store your full card or bank details' is scoped to the object of
the denial and not to the whole sentence. A tell that is too narrow makes a future denial UNSCOPEABLE
(which FAILS); a tell that is too broad makes it INTERSECT (which FAILS). Neither direction passes
quietly, which is why erring is safe here and guessing is not.

ip_address.what: The network address a request came from, in a form that still identifies the connection. Personal data under GDPR and India's DPDP. ⚠️ GlitchTip's `scrub_ip_addresses` flag ANONYMISES (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64) and then STORES — an anonymised prefix is still this category, which is exactly why the flag reading `True` hid the breach for weeks.

ip_fingerprint.what: A salted, one-way fingerprint of a network address, used as an abuse counter key and discarded within the hour. A DIFFERENT category from ip_address on purpose, and the published page draws the same line ('The fingerprint is not reversible to an IP address'). The construction is keyed (crypto.subtle.sign), not a digest — an unsalted sha256 of an IPv4 address is reversible by exhausting 2^32 values and would BE the address wearing a hash.

crash_report.what: An exception, its stack trace and the app/platform/version context around it. Received by GlitchTip, which we run ourselves.

usage_event.what: One record that a feature of an app was used, written only after consent.

install_identifier.what: The random per-install identifier (`anon_id`) that makes usage records pseudonymous rather than anonymous. Not a name, not an email, not an advertising ID — but stable, so records from one installation group together.
tells: random identifier created on your device

approximate_location.what: Country, region and city, derived at the network edge from an address that is then discarded. Coarse by construction; it is not a coordinate.

consent_record.what: The append-only record that a consent decision was made: which install, when, granted or withdrawn, and which policy version was shown.

email_address.what: A plain email address, as typed. Held by the launch-notification signup list, and present verbatim inside a merchant-of-record notification.

buyer_billing_details.what: The buyer's name and billing country, as they arrive inside a merchant-of-record notification stored VERBATIM ([pipeline 5]M-2 — a re-serialised or redacted copy can never be re-verified against the signature it came with).

entitlement_record.what: What a person has paid for: one row per (user, app, entitlement).

account_identifier.what: The account id a row is keyed on (a Supabase `sub`, or a store/aggregator user id). Not a credential.

user_content.what: What a person created inside an app — for apps/subly, the subscriptions they track and their budget figures. User-entered content about their own finances.
tells: what you created inside an app

payment_instrument.what: A card or bank number, CVV, IBAN or equivalent — the instrument itself. NOTHING in this factory receives this category, and no migration may declare a column for one (asserted separately by the `full card or bank details` claim row in policy-claims.json).

_why: 🔴 THE HALF THAT MAKES THE DENIAL LIMB UNFAKEABLE, and it is DATA rather than a list inside the guard
for exactly the reason `nonProviderRouteSegments` is. The guard extracts every "we do not collect /
do not store X" clause from the visible text of the published pages. A denial is allowed to exist
only if it resolves to a category in `dataCategories` above — or is written down HERE with a reason.
So publishing 'we do not store your precise location' turns the build RED until somebody either adds
the category (and therefore has to say whether a live sink receives it) or classifies the sentence as
not being about a data category at all. There is no third option, and no way to pad this list except
by naming the sentence you are adding.
⚠️ A row here is checked in BOTH directions: one whose denial no longer appears on its page FAILS, so
an exemption cannot outlive the sentence it was granted for — the same rule `disclosureGaps` carry
through `stillTrue`. And a row that DOES resolve to a category FAILS as inert: an exemption for
something that is not there reports judgement over nothing.

rows.denial: do not knowingly collect personal information from them
rows.why: §7, children's privacy. This denies collecting anything at all FROM A CLASS OF PERSON (under 13, or the local minimum age) — it is scoped by WHO, not by WHAT. Scoping it against a sink's category list would be a category error in the literal sense: every category would intersect it, and the guard would go red on a sentence that is true. The duty it belongs to is age-assurance, which is carried as a row in tooling/legal/duty-matrix.json where the trigger can be stated.

providers.name: Apple App Store
providers.privateRecord: OWNER_QUEUE A-4 — the Apple Developer account. Deferred by the owner; no account exists.
notes: Named by its full store name in privacy.html §3 and refund.html §1. ⚠️ NOT in terms.html: §4 says
'that store's terms (Apple, Google, Microsoft)' — a parenthetical reference to the companies, not a
naming of the stores as sellers. The distinction was found by this register's own disclosure check
and the row was corrected to match the page rather than the page assumed to match the row.
Carried as a row because the pages name it, and a register that omits a named provider cannot be
the answer to 'who is in the payment path'.

providers.name: Google Play
providers.privateRecord: OWNER_QUEUE A-3 — the Play publisher account.
notes: Named in privacy.html and refund.html; terms.html says only 'Google' in a parenthetical.
tooling/channel-register.json android-play is served:false.
⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-05 — this note said 'No account yet'. The Play ORGANIZATION account has been
verified since 2026-08-04; see company/vendors/google.md. `status` stays "deferred", which is a
statement about REVENUE and is still true: zero apps published, so nothing has ever been sold
through this provider. The account and the revenue are two different facts, and only one of them
was wrong. Compare microsoft-store below, which makes no account claim and so never went stale.

providers.name: Microsoft Store
providers.privateRecord: OWNER_QUEUE A-2 — the Partner Center publisher account.
notes: Named in privacy.html and refund.html; terms.html says only 'Microsoft' in a parenthetical.
tooling/channel-register.json windows-store is served:false.

providers.name: Cloudflare
providers.receivesBasis: Derived from tooling/legal/data-inventory.json, which enumerates every D1 table, KV namespace and Pages-Function binding in this factory and marks each `personalData` true or false — all 19 of them are Cloudflare. `crash_report` is deliberately NOT in this list: crash reports land on oracle-cloud, which is the `crash-reports-infrastructure` gap privacy.html still gets wrong. `payment_instrument` is deliberately not here either, and no migration may declare a column for one.

transits.ip_address: Cloudflare IS the network edge — it terminates TLS, so the client address is inherent in the connection and cannot not be seen. It is not retained for us: the events path derives country/region/city from `request.cf` and discards the address (privacy.html discloses exactly this), and the signup path keeps a keyed one-way fingerprint rather than the address. ⚠️ THIS IS THE ESCAPE ROUTE FROM THE DENIAL LIMB AND IT IS NAMED AS ONE — moving a category from `receives` to `transits` silences the intersection check. It is a visible edit in a diff and it PRINTS on every run, but it is a declaration about a sink no repo-resident guard can observe.

notes: The only LIVE provider in this register. Hosts both static sites (Git integration), both Workers,
D1 and KV. privacy.html discloses it as the hosting provider and as the network edge — both true.
⚠️ The SECOND sentence naming Cloudflare in privacy.html is not true, and it is carried as the
`crash-reports-infrastructure` disclosureGap below rather than being fixed here: fixing it means
editing a published page.

providers.name: Paddle
providers.privateRecord: OWNER_QUEUE A-1 — the Paddle seller application, KYC and payout account. [ADR 004] holds the decision itself; [ADR 039] holds which channels it is the rail for.
notes: 🔒 LOCKED as the primary merchant of record by [ADR 004] on 2026-07-23, and SCOPED by [ADR 039] on
2026-08-09: Paddle is the rail for every channel with no store tax — the web, the Microsoft Store
(Store Policies v7.19 §10.8.1/§10.8.6 permit a third-party purchase API for non-game PC apps at no
Store Fee), Windows/macOS/Linux direct downloads, Snap and APK sideload. Apple and Google Play use
their own billing, so Paddle is NOT the seller there. `packages/purchases/lib/src/
purchase_capabilities.dart` carries the same split with the same citations, per channel.
[ADR 039] D6 also settles INDIA, which is why the pages can say 'in every country we sell to,
including India' rather than hedging: Paddle Billing ships India UPI AutoPay (renders on country=IN
+ INR checkouts; ₹15k recurring cap, our SKUs well under) and Paddle registers and remits Indian
OIDAR GST itself. ⚠️ THE UPI DETAIL IS RECORDED HERE AND DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED: the ADR's own
rider is 'live-verify UPI renders for THIS account when checkout opens', so which payment METHODS a
buyer sees is an unverified vendor fact, while WHO THE SELLER IS is a decided one. The pages carry
the second and not the first.
NAMED IN terms.html §4 AND refund.html §2/§4 since this change; both describe the role (legal
seller, takes the payment, remits the tax) and say the receipt names the contracting Paddle entity.
privacy.html still says only 'a merchant of record' — that is the narrowed `merchant-of-record-
unnamed` gap below, and it stays open because privacy.html is version-gated.
⚠️ `status` STAYS `not-yet-applied`, AND NAMING PADDLE DID NOT CHANGE IT. The status is about the
SELLER ACCOUNT (OWNER_QUEUE A-1, private-SSoT material this file may not record), not about the
disclosure. The pages are written in the future tense for exactly that reason — 'we do not sell
anything directly from this website today; this is the arrangement that will apply when we do' —
so nothing published here asserts an account that does not exist. The day the row goes `live` the
both-pages rule in assert-policy-claims.mjs §3(c) is already satisfied instead of newly owed.

providers.name: Lemon Squeezy
notes: 🔴 THE PARALLEL BET IS RETIRED. [ADR 039] D4 (2026-08-09): the 'apply to Lemon Squeezy in parallel'
clause of [ADR 004] is withdrawn — it was never evidenced, and the product is strategically
sunsetting under the Stripe acquisition. `privateRecord` dropped its A-1 pointer with it: there is
no application to point at.
⚠️ THE ROW IS KEPT AND `status` STAYS `deferred`, WHICH IS A DECISION ABOUT THIS GUARD AND NOT A
HEDGE. assert-policy-claims.mjs §3(c) treats `deferred` as deliberately silent and every other
non-live status as 'being pursued, so the missing disclosure is a real gap that prints'. A retired
bet is the first kind, not the second: printing 'the backup merchant of record is not named in our
terms' on every CI run would be printing the absence of a decision nobody is taking. The row itself
survives for the reason tooling/channel-register.json keeps rows for channels we do not serve — the
researched facts are recorded once instead of rediscovered under time pressure, and a deletion
would leave the retirement invisible.
Paddle-concentration risk is real and [ADR 039] D4 grades it medium-high (termination / fund-hold
class). The `MoRWebhookVerifier` seam makes a fallback a config change, but WHICH successor
(FastSpring / Polar / Creem / direct Stripe + a tax engine) is a queued owner decision and is
deliberately not answered by putting a name in this row.

providers.name: Razorpay
notes: WAS NAMED IN TWO PUBLISHED PAGES AND REACHABLE FROM NO CODE; the naming has been removed and the
code was never there. Until this change terms.html §4 said website purchases 'are processed
securely by Razorpay' and refund.html §2/§4 routed website refunds through it, while privacy.html
said we do not sell anything directly from this website at all. There is no Razorpay integration
anywhere in this repository — no route, no key, no webhook — so the pages named a payment path
that did not exist, for a purchase the same site said does not happen.
A gateway is also the WRONG SHAPE for what [ADR 004] decided: a gateway leaves US the seller and
leaves the worldwide sales-tax duty with us, which is the exact burden a merchant of record was
chosen to remove.
🔒 AND [ADR 039] D6 (2026-08-09) SETTLED IT ON MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN PREFERENCE: as a payment
aggregator Razorpay makes NIKATRU the domestic seller in India — net ~82% of sticker after our own
18% GST, against ~92.5% via Paddle on the annual SKU, plus a recurring B2C GST filing surface. That
is why the India clause on the pages names Paddle and not a domestic rail. RAZORPAY IS NOT THE APP
RAIL. Its recorded scope is unchanged by that lock and is narrow: a nikatru.com website-domestic
gateway, dashboard-hosted, with ZERO code in this repository.
⚠️ THE ROW IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED so the removal is a recorded fact instead of an absence. If
the revisit trigger in [ADR 039] D6 ever fires (web-India above ~100 sales/month, or measurably
poor Paddle UPI acceptance) and a domestic rail is offered alongside the merchant of record, THIS
is the row that goes back to `namedIn` — and note that the both-pages rule in
assert-policy-claims.mjs applies to the merchant of record and NOT to a gateway, so nothing would
catch that silently. The re-disclosure is a human duty and this paragraph is where it is written.
⚠️ WHETHER A RAZORPAY MERCHANT ACCOUNT EXISTS IS NOT RECORDED HERE and must not be: account state
is private-SSoT material (see the ⚠️ note at the top of this file). `not-named-not-wired` is a
statement about this repository and the published pages, and about nothing else.

providers.name: RevenueCat
notes: 🔴 THE ONLY PROVIDER IN THIS REGISTER THAT REAL CODE REACHES, AND IT IS NAMED IN NO PAGE.
services/subly-api/src/routes/webhooks.ts mounts POST /v1/webhooks/revenuecat, authenticated by a
shared secret and fail-closed when the secret is unset. It upserts rows into platform_db
`entitlements` keyed on a RevenueCat app_user_id.
It is `wired-not-live` rather than `live` because no store account exists to send it an event:
every kind:store row in tooling/channel-register.json is served:false. The route works; nothing
calls it. That is precisely why it is easy to leave undisclosed until the day it matters.
🔒 [ADR 039] D5 LOCKED RevenueCat as the mobile-store IAP glue (2026-08-09) — one SDK for both
stores, hosted receipt and lifecycle handling, native Paddle Billing integration so every rail
resolves to ONE entitlement answer; $0 to $2,500 MTR, then 1% of tracked revenue. It enters the
codebase properly at the Play-Billing increment and at A-4; until then it is a dependency-in-
waiting with a built, dormant, bearer-verified, fail-closed webhook.
🔴 `role` STAYS `iap_aggregator` AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART OF THIS ROW. RevenueCat is NOT a
merchant of record and must never be recorded as one: the store is the seller for a store purchase
and Paddle is the seller everywhere else, while RevenueCat only normalises the resulting purchase
events into one entitlement feed. The register's own vocabulary draws the line — `iap_aggregator`
is 'holds purchase state, not payment instruments', `merchant_of_record` is 'the legal seller'. If
this row's role were ever flipped, assert-policy-claims.mjs §3(c) would immediately start demanding
that terms.html and refund.html name RevenueCat as a seller, which would be a false disclosure the
guard had asked for. Locked here in prose because no guard can hold a definition for us.
It holds an `account_identifier` (the RevenueCat app_user_id) and `entitlement_record` data, so the
disclosure duty is privacy.html's third-party list, not the buyer-facing seller pages — carried as
the `iap-aggregator-unnamed` gap below.

providers.name: Supabase
notes: The auth vendor. services/platform/wrangler.jsonc declares SUPABASE_URL and the brick's
initNikatruAuth wires it; [ADR 005] holds the persistence decision and [ADR 024] the app's
auth-init exception. No shipped app creates accounts today — the brick's default is
needs_backend:false — so nothing is stored under it yet.
Named in no page. privacy.html's third-party section lists stores, Cloudflare and 'a merchant of
record' and does not mention an identity provider. Carried as the `identity-provider-unnamed`
gap: it becomes a disclosure duty the day an app actually offers accounts, and that day is a
declared trigger in tooling/legal/duty-matrix.json rather than a memory.

providers.name: Oracle Cloud
providers.privateRecord: company/runbooks/glitchtip.md — the self-hosted GlitchTip instance and its operations.
providers.receivesBasis: 🔴 THIS ROW IS WHY THE SINK-DISCLOSURE LIMB EXISTS. Until 2026-08-06 this sink ALSO received `ip_address`, while privacy.html published 'We do not collect or store your IP address' — and nothing in this repository could see it, because the only personal-data store outside Cloudflare appears in no inventory here. Fixed at the sink and verified BY OBSERVATION, not by reading a setting (knowledge/session-notes.md §17): two layers, because either alone is a false fix. (1) The sink refuses — 12 IP keys added to GlitchTip's `sensitive_keys`, which is what catches a CLIENT-SUPPLIED address; tested with 203.0.113.45. (2) Nothing is collected — nginx blanks the 11 client-IP headers in python_ipware's precedence tuple, so `get_client_ip` falls through to the Docker gateway and returns None. Probed after: no `user` object at all on a fresh event; the negative control against the pre-change config returned the address unmodified, so the assertion can fail. The 18 back-catalogue events holding a real address were redacted in place, non-destructively.

transits.ip_address: An ingest request necessarily arrives from the device's address; that is TCP, not a choice. Nothing writes it — see `receivesBasis`. ⚠️ AND THIS IS EXACTLY THE DECLARATION A REPO-RESIDENT GUARD CANNOT CHECK. If somebody re-enables IP storage on the live GlitchTip without editing this line, every guard in this repository stays green. Only a probe against the live GlitchTip API can close that, and no such probe exists today: the compose file lives at /opt/glitchtip on the box and is in no tree CI can read.

notes: Crash reports go to a GlitchTip instance we run ourselves on an Oracle Cloud always-free VM.
privacy.html says crash reports run 'on infrastructure provided by Cloudflare'. That sentence is
wrong about this provider — see the `crash-reports-infrastructure` gap. The rest of the same
paragraph (that crash reports are NOT sent to a third-party analytics product, and are received by
software we run ourselves) is true and stays true under either host.

providers.name: Resend
providers.privateRecord: company/vendors/resend.md — the account, the API key and the sending domain. The SMTP wiring itself is recorded in company/vendors/supabase.md ([ADR 029]).
notes: 🔴 THIS ROW IS A FOUND DISCLOSURE GAP, AND THE FINDING IS THAT THERE WAS NO GAP ROW. Resend has
delivered every Supabase auth email since auth mail went live — smtp.resend.com, sending as
auth@mail.nikatru.com ([ADR 029]) — so it has held every user's email address that whole time. It
appeared in NEITHER this register NOR sites/nikatru/privacy.html until 2026-08-10. The other four
privacy.html corrections signed that day each had a `disclosureGaps` row printing on every CI run;
this one had nothing, because a provider absent from the register is absent from everything the
register drives. That is the difference between a gap that is TRACKED and a gap that is INVISIBLE,
and it is recorded here rather than quietly closed: nothing in this repository would have raised
it, and nothing in this repository will raise the next one either. The guards check the list
against the pages, never the list against reality — adding a vendor without adding its row is
still a silent hole, and only a person comparing the two closes it.
It is deliberately NOT in retiredDisclosureGaps: no gap row ever existed, and inventing one would
fabricate a history in which the omission was known and scheduled. It was not.
⚠️ SCOPE BOUNDARY, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR COVERAGE: assert-sink-disclosure.mjs quantifies
over `infrastructure` rows with status `live`, and this row is `email_delivery`. The categories
Resend holds are therefore NOT checked against the published denials by that guard. The role is
the right one — Resend hosts nothing — and borrowing `infrastructure` to pick up the limb would be
putting a false claim in the register to satisfy a check. What DOES bind is assert-policy-claims
.mjs: `namedIn` forces this row's tells to appear in privacy.html's visible text on every run, so
the disclosure cannot silently disappear once made.
TRANSACTIONAL ONLY. The privacy sentence names sign-in and account-verification messages and claims
no marketing channel, because there is none: ConsentPurpose.marketingEmail is collection-only, with
no sender and no list ([ADR 040] decision 5). Describing a channel we do not operate would be a
promise to keep true for nothing.

retiredDisclosureGaps._note: 🔴 RETIRED, NOT DELETED — 2026-08-10, by the owner signature that bumped sites/nikatru/privacy.html to version 2026-08-10. All four were live rows in `disclosureGaps` until that commit, and each one is a sentence that was WRONG or MISSING on a published legal page for weeks; deleting the record would delete the only evidence of how long. assert-policy-claims.mjs reads `disclosureGaps` ONLY, so nothing in this array is checked — which is exactly why each row carries `closedBy`, naming the span that now says the true thing and the tooling/legal/policy-claims.json row that pairs it. If a future edit drops one of those spans, THAT row fails; this list is a record, not a guard, and does not pretend to be one.

Usage statistics do run on Cloudflare. Crash reports run on an Oracle Cloud VM, so the sentence covered two systems on two providers and was wrong about the second.
